# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) and
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable, independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates in the body of RFC-039 are the sole authority; this document
> is responsible only for decomposition to executable granularity and registration of conflicts that
> have not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                               |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each of which can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                           |

**Reserved numbering (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the
LALRPOP route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unassigned (2026-11-25). None of
these three has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the full history of this
document has zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and there are no repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05`
(test revival and completion): that phase has been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's
numbering remains aligned with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding of
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered here**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the justification for phase
ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 rows **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning Phase**” (the P to which the task truly belongs, which may differ
from its containing section) and “**Blocks the mainline**”; `registered, awaiting scheduling` is no
longer the default state, and an unmarked task is considered **not schedulable**. Numbering must be
**unique throughout the document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and
must not occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable), written on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write the fix,
the criteria chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**: those
belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board, not a process diary.
**Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “user decision A/B/C,” “Proposal A,”
“Option A,” and “the final implementation is…” must not appear here—the board answers only
“completed or not”; consult the commit message and RFC-039 decision registry for decisions and
outcomes.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after push**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push has completed. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see “short hash is taken after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself has no hash—self-reference
is impossible.

**The count column contains only numbers**: the Level 1/2/3 counts under “Positioning and Scope”
contain only current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Resolution                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split; `01-routing.md`'s directory tree contains one mention of `annotations.rs`, the only such mention in the entire batch                                                                                                          | P5's steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                   |
| G2  | **The three ownership assignments for the `include!` refactor have no implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` also lists it under S7. However, `02`'s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                              | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here                |
| G3  | **Three parallel lists of CI scripts coexist**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists another 4 checks (all with different names); `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (the script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified list (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents reference this table                   |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                                |
| G5  | **Conflict in the L2 goal statement**: RFC-039 and the index of this directory once said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | It has been consolidated into a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent; do not pad endlessly; do not
patch what should be refactored) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, while reviving tests in P1, work will already be adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Approach)

Source: defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 ＋ **Audit of
silent-discard points on 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or any
> subsequent phase discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A
> silent failure / B silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack
> overflow, silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactoring**, but
> all four requirements must be met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and
> genuinely fail); ② no change to the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously
> compiled successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and existing diagnostic
> codes / prose / exit codes must not be removed or modified); ③ registration in the same commit
> (this row identifies the error type + a revision note for that phase + the PR's required “Error
> Type” field); ④ regeneration of the baseline in the same commit + manual review of the diff. **D
> user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes** must still be
> adjudicated first. See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md)
> for the expanded criteria and A–F allowlist; **“default to a super-refactor and register it
> afterward” is not accepted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes
> cannot be distinguished from regressions, and this conflicts with both “no C5′” and “no relaxation
> whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: defect criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn them red
again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 to the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and P9's 9.2 gate as the criterion. **Risk**: the
new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus-differential
baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential, performance baseline) may
> proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness defects (`Sorted(3)` passing silently) must not
> be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3 (panic to diagnostic) has no prerequisites
> and may be implemented at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
an ordering constraint**. It is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of all
four refactoring phases; reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and baseline updates
on the new grammar / checker layout / SSA IR.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                      | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`      | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→true `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branch will be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                                                              |
| Dead-code exemption `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `semantic_tokens`' `Public` modifier                               | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first land a red criterion before
   code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, they must be replaced by
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (the new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ the
   corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG are updated in
   the same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be sequential
and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to start based on the context at hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter + the
> main-chain/constraint row) was included in `97071c81b` while RFC-039's D56 was being consolidated
> during the parallel-stream cleanup of the workspace—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary
> registration + D57/D58 decisions recorded” and does not mention this track. History is not
> rewritten; following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, as noted in the P2
> implementation note), it is registered in place as a retrospective bisection reference.

|                                                   | 4.4.4 The SMT shared-solver observation ledger `ConsumerStats`/`CONSUMER_STATS`: every production-path point writes to it, while the production side has zero readers (the only reader is `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs`). **Decision ① from 2026-10-24: retain it**—write “the sole consumer = tests” as a documentation contract (preserving the observable-criterion carrier required by D58); decision ② “delete it” is not taken (doing so would require rewriting 4.4.2's acceptance criterion at the same time, and the trade-off rationale is in the 4.4 closure “Sixteen”). **Terminal state**: the three contract sentences are written into the module header of `src/frontend/core/typecheck/proof/smt/backend.rs` and the related item's documentation comments—① write surface = each acquisition through the shared interface performs one atomic increment; ② the read surface is **only** `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs` (zero calls from production code); ③ `SolverConsumer::ALL` is a **test-only constant**, and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavioral changes** (only comments are changed, and 4.4.2's acceptance number is unchanged; issue [#475](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/475)) |                                                   | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with a **named argument** loses its formal-name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure period): a cross-unit (registry-injected) method called with a named argument reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (the old behavior was not success: after silently dropping the named argument, the call failed at runtime or returned the wrong value silently). **Scope (final form after two rounds of narrowing on 2026-11-26—only three items are added; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—by the definition unit's qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]`, obtain the declaration-time formal names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mixed-in IR name ↔ formal name are three aligned vectors, from the same source as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`'s qualified name to look up the name table rather than two bare-name segments. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (where `local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate-injection surface retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate the “same input, multiple results” behavior caused by HashMap iteration order**, not a fix for the original bug; the criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed for the same method key; removing the ascending merge produces two results). **Criteria (red before green)**: 2 driver-level tests (`src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs`: bare import with one candidate = 6.0 / two candidates selected by name = 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header carries the pathology gate); unit test in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (`method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, positive control returns a non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the deterministic criterion above). Project fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus-differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to direct parent `ac810e97`, 405→404** (an intermediate state once included `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change is an inevitable consequence of fixtures entering and leaving (`corpus_probe` regenerated and byte-for-byte identical to the checked-in baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② should-have-reported-but-did-not, Class A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declarations / named nested function declarations / built-in container constructors other than `len` with named arguments / whole-module imports / the RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected according to P0's measured semantics**: ① the **static-function form** (both within one unit and across units, declaration form and binding form) is currently **entirely unavailable**—within one unit, `check` reports E3006; across units in declaration form, `run` reports E6007; across units in binding form, `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code and are unrelated to named arguments, so this is not “the named argument was silently discarded”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table; this is also unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Class A incidental fix: the old E6007/E1014 behavior was not success, and no previously successful program now fails)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② the **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). These previously either silently dropped the argument at runtime with E6007 or falsely rejected it during `check` with `E1014 (available: )`; all now enter the slot according to the declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion in `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file's header pathology gate). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which is closed: the unit's own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the unit's own declaration) **has been closed with the import-surface consolidation in 4.9.10-S2a** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is green); the remaining item is function-body-level / cross-scope imports merged globally by unit (a shared import table)—this form does not work in the first place (an existing defect: `check` passes, `run` reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and was not fixed. **Deleted in this round (relative to the first six rounds of 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider priority, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “no name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution points**—the latter rejects mixed/alias-only forms that actually ran on the parent commit (Class D), and the decision was withdrawn on 2026-11-26; **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, `checker.rs` **must then**
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains byte-for-byte unchanged;
as measured, 5.3 **did not move it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines long—that
increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields no decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when their files grow back to 1,500
lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: the end state of D62 is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions
> share one set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> the implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is **pure
> judgment** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables); evidence is
> the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals / value environment / single-value
> pinning / Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for both closed
> and open/recursive terms); Σ construction sites **reuse the same evidence interface** rather than
> establishing another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that the names of
> the substages have been completed.**

> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require

> may run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D's
> implementation waits for confirmation of B's design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1
> (dispatch), and may depend on 6.9.3's typed exit. **The P7 gate = the A/B/C exits**; D does not
> block.

> **A.C3's prerequisite: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old
> statement “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly`
> have been deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no
> request is created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold
> `k-1`. **The adjudication changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1's second field and C-2's recovery from IR
> both break the single representation/evaluator, C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing
> pushes the recursive chain to `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: fold the condition within the
> instance / T-b: bounded firing + fall back to the original at the boundary / T-c: a termination
> layer or change the specification). **Measure first, then adjudicate; before measurement, “A is
> implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3,
> F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and the complete I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d's prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 states “the
> decision point first follows the unified path; after unified failure, equality may be used, but
> all partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (without unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; and do unify and defeq share one
> budget or have one each. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtyping /
> Any / Never; defeq only judges equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional
> subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and
> production call graph before writing code**; 6.9.3c's wiring contract wasted two rounds because it
> assumed `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` had zero production
> instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or an item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ idempotence of the error-code generator (if an emission point / code table
> changes); ④ classification of behavioral changes under D59 and red before green. **Wiring tasks
> additionally require**: evidence from the production call graph (which production entry point, how
> many paths, which path is reachable); using unit-test reachability as a substitute for user
> reachability is prohibited; rollback and budget must have measured values. **Residual
> disposition**: #537 (Class D, silent discard of proof-function parameter refinement; do not fix
> before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; Class
> C stage boundary, and if it remains unclosed, 6.9.4 covers only module-internal forms), #540
> (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on 2026-11-14: orchestrator-layer 64MB
> large-stack thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019, see the 3.20.30 row in 09),
> #541 (TailCall; **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three locations advanced and retreated together:
> `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover
> `Call`/`TailCall` through the single-point `rewritten_call_target`, and the init section and
> function bodies share one call-site rewriting mechanism; red→green + 3 mutations), #542 (orphaned
> shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two-entry wiring + removal of the C2c
> temporary avoidance; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), #552
> (imported multi-parameter predicate proof execution; a neighboring area of 6.9.5, separate case).
> **Ownership awaiting adjudication**: the four open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in
> `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4's constant-equality bridge; whether to leave
> them in 6.9.4 outOfScope or reassign them to 6.9.1 / the E4018 proof-function surface requires
> adjudication.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim the complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 only handles constant equalities and does
> not fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; `f(y)(y)`'s second value position is outside
> this item; witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 only cover
> forms that do not depend on proof-function parameter refinement; if #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4
> covers only module-internal forms; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 has landed (2026-11-19); 2.1.4's
> inner-isolation red was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten around slot identity in
> the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for elevating `verify` to a gate have been removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**2026-10-27 revision, following 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change, but
each must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted, and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is a
separate, individually adjudicated round.

> **Revision relationship**: the original wording (2026-10-26 decision ②) was
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying zero-difference requirements to all of `tests/`; this
> wording **changes only direct-drive test files from “zero difference” to “modifiable but
> registered with file / line count / reason”**, while the zero-difference requirements for the
> **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library
> (`src/std/`)** remain unchanged. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs`
> changed, with **3 lines** changed (2 occurrences of `assert_format_eq` from `i64`→`Int64` + 1
> comment line), the reason = the expected type-name spelling in the assertion must be synchronized
> with the changed spelling; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6 6.1
> Name-Normalization Closure.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer silently changes
associativity (without an error, only the parse result changes). The defenses are the permanent
D1–D3 assertions and the operator-property cross-validation test; every new operator must enter both
the table and the cross-validation test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on `08`'s D0/D2**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code references `sema` in reverse, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping correctness defects must not be blocked by criteria-infrastructure
> construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all three
> layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x is precisely the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must **be written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes the bugs to be fixed into the phase table as “established behavior”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, checker layout, and IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise, regressions cannot be located through bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the phase A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completion of 6.9.4); D (Σ) does not block. P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite for P7, is not subject to this gate, and must not consume the undecided defeq / quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5's snapshot baseline and 9.3's `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                  | Members                                                                               | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                               | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs. `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                          |
| B                                      | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                         | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| C                                      | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                       | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D                                      | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                        | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                            |
| E                                      | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                                 | After 4.1 completes, they do not depend on one another                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| F                                      | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced under P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5's snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| G                                      | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                          | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies 2 `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Non-parallelizable (overlapping files)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5
same-batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be sequential).

**New internal constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly sequential; 7.0 → 7a→7b→7c→7d
is strictly sequential (7.0 is P7's prerequisite pure-move batch), and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede
7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc inspection,” while rules
  are “pre-hoc judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching what should be refactored”; only
  D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original gap G3's three parallel lists
  made closure impossible. After consolidation, the 10 active scripts each belong to one phase (9.8
  was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), and report-only status and hardening timing are explicit
  and traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactoring means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar,
  checker layout, and IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and
  RFC-status corrections into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed the granularity at which changes can
  be rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero call-site changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it merely states that “fixed
  defects should not be rolled back,” without requiring a record of what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the name of the fixed test and a
  description of the defect, as a retrospective bisection reference.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse-grained**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse-grained**—approximately 89 renamed references, and missing one silently
  changes associativity.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34's opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, while the
  deletion action remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “separate issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left for future implementation.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

| C2              | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs. table-driven implementation                         | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + same-source cross-validation of the two `BinOp` sets (the LALRPOP route was withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification                   | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require equivalence criteria, only regression tests); C6 is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                          |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                        | **No allowlist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                             |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4's 4.2.7 has made this a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                   |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                                 | **The wasm-path defect fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                 |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assign it to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                        |
| C8              | Fixing `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number                                 | **Fix + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                           |
